subject: platform/uitest
professional: a senior QA / test-infrastructure engineer (Playwright class) who owns a CI e2e suite and judges a runner by its false-pass and false-fail rates, exit-code contract and report formats

evidence.correctness: Ran the CLI against 7 hand-built pages and the repo fixture (PLAYWRIGHT=/opt/node-tools/node_modules/playwright/index.js). Right: uncaught setTimeout throw -> fail exit 1; fixture app steps (35x10 ft, 2 coats -> '2 gallons') pass; broken.html found by --crawl 3 with 'undefinedFunction is not defined' -> exit 1; goal with no key -> skipped; 404 on a fetch -> warn only (documented default); inert page -> 'text never changed' warn but pass (documented limit). Wrong: a page whose button writes 'Total: NaN' and one that writes 'Error: failed to save' both get 'pass: smoke check passed' (exit 0), so the keyless smoke check has no NaN/undefined/error-banner detection. Reasoned-from-docs expected output matched on all other cases.
evidence.completeness: Checked README claims: smoke 4xx/5xx and blank (code present, see verification); JS errors fail; request failures warn/fail; scripted steps (fill/select/check/click/expectText/expectNoText/expectUrl/screenshot) all exercised by browser.test.mjs and fixture; --serve, --start/--wait-for, --crawl, --workers, --only, --out (report.json, junit.xml, summary.md, screenshots); exit codes 0/1/2/3 (test 28 plus CLI tests); agent loop via fake OpenAI-compatible server. Not exercised live: the real Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini providers (no key), the GitHub Action and GitLab snippet (action.yml read only). Limits section honestly lists no upload, drag and drop, Chromium only.
evidence.verification: node --test platform/uitest/*.test.mjs: 28 tests, 23 pass, 5 skip (browser.test.mjs skips because ESM import('playwright') does not resolve with Playwright in /opt/node-tools, though require() does). With PLAYWRIGHT set, browser.test.mjs: 5 pass, 0 skip. Mutations (reverted by git checkout): ignore hardIssue in judge -> 3 tests failed (caught); skipped===total -> 2 failed (caught); status>=400 -> >=500 -> 1 failed (caught); remove the blank-page check in explore.mjs -> 0 failed (SURVIVED: no test covers the blank-page fail). 3 of 4 caught.
evidence.craft: Read uitest.mjs, lib/run.mjs, explore.mjs, steps.mjs, report.mjs, server.mjs, browser.mjs (first 60 lines). Small, single-purpose modules; dependency-injected launch/ask makes it testable with fakes; safePath guards traversal; XML control characters stripped in JUnit; per-scenario fresh browser context; cleanup in finally. Defects: crawl state (crawlBudget, seen, queue) is shared mutable across workers without a lock (benign on single-threaded JS but order dependent); screenshots on failure swallowed with empty catch; 'nothing changed' heuristic compares whole visible text; SKIP_BUTTON regex skips any button named e.g. 'Close' or 'Cancel' with no report that coverage was skipped.
evidence.claims: README 'Why agent-driven' says the agent 'fails on wrong numbers, NaN, error banners' (true only with a model key and a run that visits it); Smoke row says it fills, clicks and warns, which is accurate, but a reader of the first paragraph ('also does the checks that need no AI ... dead pages and forms that render but never respond') would expect NaN pages to fail keyless: they pass (verified). 'Playwright resolved as playwright' is false for ESM when installed outside the project (tests skip silently, 5 of 28). 'Keys never appear in reports' not independently checked (platform/llm not audited). Backed: exit codes, --help numbers (test 28), flags, file layout of --out, MIT/no telemetry (no network code outside byok).
evidence.fitness: Walked a QA lead's job: point at a static build, get JUnit plus screenshots, fail CI on JS errors and dead pages, add scripted steps for exact checks, optional agent goals. Did it on the fixture with one command and got a correct report and exit code. Missing for a real suite: no retries/flake handling, no traces/video, no auth/storage-state reuse, no assertions beyond text/URL (no element state, no network assertions), no sharding. Adequate for smoke and a few key flows, not a Playwright Test replacement, and it does not claim to be.
evidence.domain: Compared with Playwright Test and its conventions: auto-waiting for expectText and the fresh-context-per-test isolation match; JUnit and exit-code contract are right; refusing top-level navigation off-origin and fencing page content as untrusted for the agent is good practice. Departures a senior would flag: negative assertions check once with no wait (documented), no retries or trace artifacts, request failures default to warn so a broken API call on a user action passes (fn3 page: POST/GET 404 after click -> pass), no content-based failure heuristics keyless (NaN/undefined/[object Object]), no accessibility or visual checks.

defects.what: Keyless smoke check passes pages that display NaN, undefined or an error banner after the click it makes (verified with hand-built pages; exit 0 'smoke check passed'). README opens by promising it catches forms that 'render but never respond' and the agent section promises NaN/error-banner failures; only agent runs with a key do.
No test covers the blank-page smoke failure: removing the check left all 28 tests green.

browser.test.mjs silently skips 5 of 28 tests when Playwright is only resolvable via CommonJS/NODE_PATH; the default invocation reports green with the browser half unrun. README says it resolves 'playwright' but only ESM resolution works.
Request failures default to warn, so a click that triggers a 404/500 API call still passes the run (documented, but a risky default for a CI gate).
SKIP_BUTTON silently skips buttons named close/cancel/buy/pay/checkout etc. with no note in the report.

verdict: A well-structured, honestly-limited Playwright-based runner: all 28 tests pass (with PLAYWRIGHT set, the browser half runs 5/5), the CLI gave correct verdicts and exit codes on the fixture and on hand-built pages, and 3 of 4 seeded mutations were caught. It does not meet the bar because of the claims gap: the keyless smoke check passes NaN and error-banner pages that the README's framing implies it catches, no test covers the blank-page failure, and the default test command silently skips the browser tests in environments like this one. A senior QA engineer would adopt it for smoke and a few flows after adding a text-heuristic check and flipping request-failures to fail.
